answer: opal escrows activation bonds in ocean, while juniper assigns keys under common control to one operator and keeps an activation tally that retirement cannot lower. Each activation locks the square of the operator’s new tally in ocean, and every earlier bond stays locked while its identity lives. One identity needs 1 ocean; ten live identities need 385 ocean simultaneously, with the final activation locking 100. Parallel sign-ups or split wallets cannot reuse collateral; an unrelated debut still needs 1.
